title: SLO noise and metrics-gap retrospective (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Summarize recent on-call incidents where SLO burn alerts fired due to missing/misaligned metrics and alert flapping. Draft of short-term mitigations and long-term runbook/run-rate changes to reduce noise and avoid false SLO violations. This is a working doc; edits welcome.

High-level summary:
- Incidents: Feb 09 2025 (INF-2143) and Feb 22 2025 — both produced SLO burn alerts for 'api_success_rate' and triggered paging for the on-call rotation.
- Impact: paging fatigue for on-call, several escalations to infra team, customer-facing SLO dashboard showed >5% error SLO burn for ~18-30 minutes in both incidents.
- Root cause (summary): intermittent metric ingestion lag (Prometheus remote_write backlog) combined with coarse SLI calculation that treats missing series as zeros, and an aggressive SLO alerting window that didn't tolerate transient ingestion delays.

Timeline (compressed):
- 2025-02-09 02:18 UTC: first SLO burn alert -> page to on-call SRE.
- 02:22 UTC: on-call confirms spike on SLO dashboard; application graphs (request rate, 5xx) show normal counts but 'api_success_rate' series shows sudden drop.
- 02:25 UTC: investigation shows Prometheus remote_write backlog growing on prometheus-02; network egress to remote store had bursty packet loss during autoscaler activity.
- 02:33 UTC: backlog drains, metrics reappear; SLO alert auto-resolves ~02:40 UTC after 20m of degradation window.
- 2025-02-22: similar pattern, different prometheus replica, longer backlog due to retention compaction job; SLO stayed in burn for ~30m.

Evidence and diagnostics collected:
- Prometheus logs: repeated "remote_write: failed to send samples" and backlog size spikes up to 150k samples.
- Grafana dashboard: request success counts stable; error rates unchanged.
- Exporter instrumentation: api service continued to emit metrics (local Prom counter increments are present).
- Network metrics: increased retransmits and transient 1–2 second egress spikes on nodes running remote-write workers.
- SLO calculation: current SLI query treats absent 'success' series as 0 -> causes downward bias when ingestion lags.

Root cause hypothesis (final):
1) Primary: Prometheus remote_write backlog due to transient network egress issues combined with compaction/IO spikes on remote-store nodes.
2) Contributing: SLI/SLO definitions assume metric presence; missing series was interpreted as failures (no guard for 'stale' series).
3) Alerting config: 5m evaluation with no smoothing + burn window caused pages for transient ingestion glitches.

Why this produced noisy/false pages:
- The SLI fused instrumentation availability and success ratio together; when instrumentation is delayed the SLI value drops dramatically even though app success rate is unchanged.
- Our alerting has little protection for "metric absence" vs "true error".
- On-call escalations were manual, no auto-suppression for known ingestion incidents.

Queries and examples (for runbook / playbook use):
- Current SLI (simplified):
  success_rate = sum(rate(api_requests{code!~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests[5m]))
  Note: if api_requests counters are missing or zeroed during backlog, this ratio returns low values.
- Detection for metric-gap (to add):
  missing_series_ratio = 1 - (count(up{job="api"}) / count(expected_targets_total))
  (or count of series for api_requests / expected series count)
- PromQL to highlight ingestion lag: 
  prometheus_remote_storage_queue_highest{job="prometheus"}
  and prom_remote_storage_samples_total - prom_remote_storage_samples_sent_total  (watch backlog growth)

Short-term mitigations (<= 72h):
- Change SLO alerting to require both: (a) SLI below threshold AND (b) evidence of real error increase (5xx rate up) or presence of downstream error logs. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2025-03-06.
- Add metric-gap detector alert: if series count for api_requests drops by >30% for >3m, mark SLO alerts as suspected-instrumentation-issue and page to observability infra (non-pager) channel first. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2025-03-05.
- Suppress SLO paging for 10m if prometheus remote_write backlog >100k samples (tunable) — route to infra-oncall smoke test channel instead. Owner: Marta. ETA: 2025-03-04.
- Update on-call checklist to include quick checks: local counters on app host, prom_remote_write backlog, recent deploys. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2025-03-03.

Long-term fixes (quarter roadmap):
- Fix remote_write resiliency: ensure remote_write has bounded memory, backoff and burst smoothing, retry jitter and better instrumentation around backlog. Cross-team with infra/observability. Linked PR: observability#789. Owner: infra team. ETA: 2025-Q2.
- Rework SLI definition: move to an "existence-protected" SLI that ignores missing series and uses fallback signals (application logs/agent counters). For example: if series missing, compute SLI from traced requests or fallback exporter. Owner: eng-sre + app teams. ETA: 2025-Q2.
- Introduce synthetic traffic and an internal heartbeat SLI (small constant requests) to detect metric ingestion gaps separate from production traffic. Owner: platform-engineering. ETA: 2025-Q3.

Runbook changes (draft):
- New diagnostic steps to add under "SLO alert: success_rate burn":
  1) Check prom_remote_write backlog: Prometheus > Metrics -> search prom_remote_storage_queue_highest.
  2) Check target series count for api_requests: if series dropped by >25% in last 10m, treat as instrumentation/ingestion issue.
  3) Check app host local counters: curl exporter on a few hosts to confirm counters increment.
  4) Check 5xx rate: if 5xx not elevated, deprioritize immediate rollback and escalate to observability infra.
  5) If ingestion confirmed, apply suppression policy (existing suppression play) and annotate incident with "suspected-metrics-gap" tag.

Pager policy updates (proposal):
- Only page on SLO burn when BOTH SLI below threshold AND either 5xx-rate/spike-in-error-traces present OR no detected ingestion-gap.
- For alerts where ingestion-gap is detected treat as "observability incident" and route to observability Slack channel and infra-oncall (non-pager) first.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the acceptable percent for series-drop that indicates ingestion issue vs partial exporter failure? (25%? 40%?) Suggest starting at 30% and adjust after testing.
- How aggressive should suppression be for remote_write backlog? If we suppress too early we risk masking real failures. Need SRE + product review.
- Should synthetic heartbeat live in hosted infra or per-customer infra for Dedicated/Private? Impact on billing and data isolation to be discussed.

Action items (concrete):
- Aisha: update runbook with diagnostic steps and sample PromQL (due 2025-03-03).
- Liam: implement AND-clause on SLO alert to require 5xx or no-ingestion flag (due 2025-03-06).
- Ethan: add metric-gap alert and dashboard panel for series counts (due 2025-03-05).
- Marta: implement suppression trigger for prom_remote_write backlog and create play to route to infra channel (due 2025-03-04).
- Infra: review remote_write tuning and open PR with changes; aim for Q2.

Notes / small experiments to run this sprint:
- Run simulated ingestion gap in staging (kill remote-write for 10m) to verify SLO alert behavior and suppression logic. Owner: observability eng.
- Add temporary annotation on SLO dashboard to show "metric-gap suspected" when series count falling. Owner: dashboards team.

Related tickets / refs:
- INF-2143 (incident log)
- OBS-112 (runbook baseline)
- PR #789 (observability remote_write improvements)

Closing notes:
This doc is intentionally a working draft to capture findings and immediate mitigations. Goal is to stop noisy pages that are distracting on-call and then implement robust SLI safeguards so customers don't see spurious SLO violations. Please add comments inline or propose edits; after consensus we'll move runbook edits to final and postmortem to INF-2143.

-- Aisha (oncall SRE)
